# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 7 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 7
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Understand this, children of joy: the good Lord showed us everything in advance, so that we would know who deserves our gratitude and praise for all things.
2. The Son of God is Lord, and he is coming to judge both the living and the dead. Yet he suffered, so that his wounds could give us life. Let us believe this: the Son of God could only have suffered for our sake.
3. At his crucifixion, they gave him vinegar and gall to drink. See how the temple priests had already prefigured this: the written command said "Whoever does not keep the fast will die." The Lord commanded this because he was about to offer the vessel of the Spirit as a sacrifice for our sins — fulfilling the type that was set up when Isaac was offered on the altar.
4. What does the prophet say? "They shall eat the goat offered on the day of the fast for all our sins." Pay attention to what follows: "And the priests alone shall eat the entrails, unwashed with vinegar."
5. Why? Because he is saying: "I am about to offer my flesh for the sins of my new people, and you will give me vinegar and gall to drink — so you alone shall eat, while the people fast and wear sackcloth and ashes." This shows that he had to suffer at their hands.
6. Notice the command: "Take two perfect, identical goats and offer them. Let the priest take one as a burnt offering for sins."
7. And the other? "The other is cursed." Look at how the type of Jesus shows up here.
8. "Spit on it, prod it, wrap scarlet wool around its head, and drive it out into the desert." The one who carries the goat out leads it to the wilderness, takes off the wool, and drapes it over a bush called rachia — the one whose young shoots we eat when we find them in the fields, because the fruit is sweet.
9. Here is what I understand this to mean: when they see him on that day with his long scarlet robe reaching to his feet, they will say, "Isn't this the one we crucified — whose garment we mocked and pierced? Yes — this one truly was the Son of God."
10. In that day he will be like them in appearance — but they will not be like him in glory.
